Oink 0.3.2 lets you use Oink at the Windows sign-in screen, and fixes images dragged into web pages on Windows and a Mac staying offline.

## New

- Use Oink at the Windows sign-in screen: when Launch at login is on, Oink also runs on Windows before anyone signs in, so you can control the sign-in screen from your other computers. Turning it on asks once for administrator approval; if it still needs approval, Settings → General shows a Grant access button next to Launch at login.
- The Windows installer now asks on its first page whether to start Oink when you sign in.

## Fixes

- Fixed images dragged from another computer into Chrome and other browsers on Windows failing to load (for example, "image failed to load" on upload pages).
- Fixed a Mac sometimes staying offline until Oink was restarted, after macOS stopped Oink's network connection (for example, when VPN or security software changed network settings).

## Compatibility

- 0.3.2 works with 0.3.1 and 0.3.0. Using the Windows sign-in screen needs 0.3.2 on that Windows computer; the computers controlling it can be on 0.3.0 or later.

## Downloads

- **Mac:** the `.dmg` file — Apple silicon, macOS 14.2 or later. Developer ID signed and notarized.
- **Windows:** the `.msi` file — x64, Windows 10 22H2 (build 19045) or later, or Windows 11. Requires the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Evergreen runtime (preinstalled on current Windows).

Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS`.

## Known limitations

- At the Windows sign-in screen, only keyboard and mouse sharing works; clipboard, files and audio start after you sign in. While you type a password with that computer's own keyboard, the keyboard cannot control other computers.
- If several Windows users turn on Launch at login, the sign-in screen uses the device identity of the user who turned it on most recently.
- Turning Oink off in Windows Settings → Apps → Startup does not stop it at the sign-in screen; turn off Launch at login in Oink instead.
- The Windows MSI is not code-signed in this release. SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC": choose **More info → Run anyway**. UAC shows an unknown publisher.
- Receiving files on a Mac requires the Oink File Provider location to be enabled; if prompted, enable it in Settings → Permissions.
- Windows users on 0.2.1 need to install the 0.2.2 bridge update before the in-app update can install 0.3.2.
